The .conf configuration format is outdated and will no longer be supported by hyprland

Change to hyprland.lua and rewrite ur config Here's their sample https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/main/example/hyprland.lua

Start by learning qml.
U only need to understand basics like components,signals,items,how to draw shapes n curves(shape path/canvas),repeater,some basic syntax and programming quirks/features of qml.

I started with https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RWd-zjclFB0&list=PLP7UmEJ9z4mpi0JXcPS0VRK-7eFAfROZI If you go with this remember to SKIP ALL THE C/C++ stuff it is NOT needed for ricing tasks.

I would instead recommend watching https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k0fyXP6YaRk&t=236s There are only 2 videos (part 1 ,part 2) dedicated purely to quickshell/qml but it is a great starting point.

Now quickshell is a framework on top of qml so there is no dedicated playlist(afaik), it is easy to say "just read the docs" but that can be exhausting I'd say just skim the docs first read whatever u find interesting and research when u need a specific feature/component.

Also the best way to learn is by observing and understanding existing projects on github notably the caelestia shell which I found to be quite neat.

If you open the caelestia shell github u can see how they have modularised the project building tiny but highly customised ui elements and combining them together whenever needed enabling reusability and clean division of components.U can ofcourse look up system design principles or project management rules somewhere but I personally find breaking down your components into small reusable parts structured properly and dedicated files for signal management and backend management to be enough. I m ofcourse a newbie so theres probably a lot more stuff to do that makes ur code easy to read and configure so u may have to do more research on this.

If u are using Ai (it can actually be pretty good for learning/syntax correction/searches) pls know that its absolutely shit at qml/quickshell and even hyprland syntax to some extent.Maybe it is because qml is relatively niche when compared to html css js etc.
But that does not mean it is not helpful, if u attach docs/discussion/proper context give good prompts and understand what u are doing it will speed up your learning process and the project by a lot.I will recommend using a tool like repomix which generates xml of ur git repositories to provide context to ai, u can ofcourse make one of a popular git repo (like caelestia) to try to understand it better.

Ai is still unreliable so ensure u have proper vcs , actually understand the project and u are looking up discussions/tutorials/projects by real humans so as to get the best results.

All the best!

[Hyprland] First Rice! (quickshell)

I had known about Linux's insane customization ability for a while, finally decided to switch around a month ago after I got my mind blown by the Caelestia shell.

I went with their stack of Hyprland + Quickshell thinking it would be easy since I have some previous experience with Linux and have done some minor frontend development (React, HTML, CSS, JS) in the past. Qt/QML was something else though, took me a while to get used to it.

Here's the stack:

Window Manager: Hyprland
Widgets/Panels/Wallpaper/Animation/Theme Switching: Quickshell
Notifications: swaync
File Manager: Thunar
App Launcher: Rofi
Music Player: rmpc and cava
System Monitor: btop
Clipboard: clipse
Idle Window: hypridle (animation is unimatrix)
Window Overview: Got lazy on this one and decided to modify files from here (great repo btw, very easy to configure)
Icons: Colorful-Dark-Icons
Background Music: 3:03 PM by Sharou

Now the animations/UI need some work and there are plenty of bugs that need fixing. For eg: while customizing Thunar I had the bright idea of writing a script that overwrites global color declarations directly in gtk.css and well, it had an interesting effect on every app not named Thunar that uses GTK CSS.

So yeah, a lot of work yet to be done. I will fix that and make the repo public later.
